Простенький примитивненький раннер косящий под аркадную классику по типу Hang One. Игровой процесс прост: едем по трассе, объезжаем прочих мотоциклистов и стараемся уложится в таймер. На этом всё. Контентно игра тоже не особо большая - 36 трасс разбитых на два режима: маршрут, где 6 трас из разных биомов и конкретно 6 трасс в одном биоме. Ну и финальный маршрут где нужно за раз проехать все 6 трасс. Так же два уровня сложности отличие в которых только в длительности таймера и том что соперники исчезают или нет при столкновении с ними. Графика простенькая, но в "супер" режиме Алисы особенно выделяются ягодицы Алисы когда она наклоняется на байке (мне её костюм почему-то напомнил плагсьют Аски из Евангелиона).

I see a lot of people saying this game is Outrun with motorcycles. I've never seen more blatant disrespect for a video game in my life. This game has nothing to do with Outrun. This game is a clear callback to Outrun's older brother, Hang-On!

Jokes and semantics aside, Super Night Riders is a modern attempt at the Super Hang-On formula, bringing it to a 3D space. It controls tightly, has a sensible driving model, and a pretty cool soundtrack. It checks the boxes, it does the job just fine. I could spend some time picking at it, how it really could use a few more environments/variations to the environments it has, how it is WAY more intense than Hang-On about how many bikes can be on the road at once, and how the Red Rider needs to be like... a centimetre shorter so I can see where the heck I'm going when I'm coming over a ridge. However, that's just picking. If you were into Hang-On on Super Hang-On, you'll be into this.

Probably something worth noting that I enjoyed was heading into the extras menu and reading the instruction manual. The bonus art you can find suggests that the dev actually was pretty into the game they were making, something I enjoy. Overall, I think Super Night Riders is pretty fun!

The core of Super Night Riders is similar to titles like Hang-On or OutRun where you thread the needle between other racers while extending your time in each stage as the course shifts into a new aesthetic. If you recognize the style from the trailer you should fully know what to expect from the whole game.

It is quite a bit more basic than I anticipated however. Closer to the first Hang-On rather than any of AM2's later titles. Transmission is automatic, there is no boosting, bumping into other racers feels very static and basic (you cannot fall off of the bike). The turning also feels a little odd almost as if it is a bit on rails at points but you get used to it. I do not mind any of this but it does make me not have any real interest in revisiting the game after I got all of the achievements.

The soundtrack is very notable and has a bit of its own style I did not anticipate. I would honestly compare it more to the Ys series before any SEGA racer, but thats just fine by me. I enjoyed every track and appreciated that you could swap between each whenever you wanted.

My only real negative with the game is that some locations have poor color combinations with the tracks and racers making it hard to make out what is ahead of you at times. Nearsighted or colorblind gamers might want to skip the game for this reason.

Super Night Riders is not as solid as SEGA's classic arcade titles, but I had a lot of fun getting all of the achievements in the span of two hours. Good for the price.

It is also worth noting that there is a remake in development, but what is here is nice for a weeknight playthrough.

Gran juego arcade de motos que nos evoca a épocas pasadas de finales de los 80, claramente inspirado en la saga Hang On de Sega. Controlamos a Alice, una motorista rubia que recorre el mundo con su moto a través de trazados plagados de curvas y otros corredores.

Al igual que en el Hang On, debemos superar tramos en cada trazado dentro del tiempo límite llegando al check point correspondiente, para obtener más tiempo y poder continuar nuestra andadura. Sencillo, pero según vayamos avanzando aparecerán cada vez más y más corredores, con lo que tendremos una mayor cantidad de obstáculos en pista.

El control es sencillo y responde bien: acelerar, frenar, y girar. Nada de controles complejos.

Las melodías son pegadizas, estilo Hang On. No llegan a ser pesadas, puesto que las podemos cambiar en plena carrera si nos hemos cansado de ellas o no nos gustan (al contrario que en el Hang On).

Recomiendo el juego, puesto que es fácil de hacerse con él, y da para unas horas de diversión si te gustan los arcades clásicos de motos.

This is one of those games where I wish I can give a 'neutral' rating. This is a fun minimalist indie title reminiscent of old racing arcade games, complete with a 32-bit polygonal aesthetic and a decent rock/electronic soundtrack. The day-to-night transitions can look really nice at times. There are no other obstacles on the race courses other than rival bikers. It's a pretty barebones game overall, but a nice time sink.

It has some majorly frustrating issues though, which became painfully clear to me as I repeatedly played the "Course 1 to 6" race.

First off, the TIME LIMIT. You have very little room to mess up. If you bump into any of the rival bikers, costing you a few precious seconds, you're already hanging by a thread in most courses. Do it a second time? You've lost already. Your bike is going to be at a max speed of 315 km/hr for 99% of the time, but there's no way to go any faster so you're guaranteed to have less than 10 seconds on the clock for the majority of your laps. There's no guarantee that the bonus time you get for completing a lap will be enough to get you through the rest of the race. But not "Course 1 to 6" though. If you bump into ANY rider, you've pretty much lost the whole race. There's no point in continuing and you'd have to restart that 36-lap race all over again. Your best chance is to memorize which specific bikers (they're all in predetermined locations) are going to give you the most trouble, then anticipate them coming (and hope for the best).

The brake is useless IMO. Just let go of the acceleration button for a second, then your steering will suddenly be better tenfold. I managed to swerve away from rival bikers in front of me this way without costing too much time. However, going through sharp turns while avoiding a whole group of bikers is not a fun time.

It can be very difficult to see other rival bikers during sunset/night stages and terrain full of trees (forest, hanami). During sunset, none of the bikers have their taillights on; the ones wearing warm colors (yellow, orange, pink) can easily blend in with the rest of the level.

Riders can suddenly pop up in front of you while you're going through sharp turns and hills (sometimes a combination of the two), giving you very little time to react. This is a dirty trick that can cost you the whole race.

This is not a bad game and it can be very fun. But it can also be incredibly frustrating for the reasons I mentioned.

[h3]Why is there even a brake button?[/h3]

This game is pretty simple: ride through 6 checkpoints while avoiding other bikes. Each checkpoint extends your time limit; run out of time and you lose. There are 6 stages (though some of them look very similar to one another) and each of the 13 courses is a combination of several stages at different times of day, with the 13th and final being a whopping 36-checkpoint long challenge.

There are two graphical settings: "classic" uses simpler 3D models and environments while "super" uses slightly prettier assets and particle effects. Soundtrack is small with only six tracks but most of them are catchy and well-suited to the game. It's possible to change BGM at any time while racing, too.

Overall I love this game so it's a thumbs up for me.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
A simple Hang-On/Super Hang-On inspired 3D arcade racer. Very straightforward classic formula. Clear checkpoints under par time to progress.

[h1]PROS:[/h1]
[list]
[*]One of the few truly Super Hang-On-like games available on PC.
[*]Two distinct visual modes. Super (more contemporary) and Classic (still 3D model based instead of sprites, but more clearly inspired by the Super Scaler graphics of yore.)
[*]Ability to select music tracks while playing.
[*]Several options for tackling tracks. (A single track at different times of day, sets of courses containing various tracks at various times of day, or - once unlocked - all 36 possible configurations from start to finish, which is the hardest and longest way to play the game.)
[*]Standard and Easy modes. (Standard is quite challenging. Easy is probably comfortable for most players, including newcomers, while still offering some challenge in later races.)
[*]Simple, intuitive controls.
[*]Online leaderboards.
[/list]

[h1]CONS:[/h1]

[list]
[*]Super Hang-On, even today, still feels a bit more nuanced than this game does in terms of handling and physics, despite its simplistic arcade nature.
[*]Nothing analogous to the Super Hang-On console release's Original Mode. Just straightforward arcade checkpoint races in succession. 
[*]Some minor input delay in menu selections (although this comes and goes, and I am not currently experiencing it at the time of this review.)
[*]Night and sunset tracks, especially those featuring particle elements, owing to the choice of lighting and colors of opponent racers, makes visibility less than optimal at times. Especially if, like me, you have poor eyesight.
[/list]

[h1]Thoughts:[/h1]

I find this to be a super enjoyable arcade racer that hearkens back to the Super Scaler days, albeit using 3D models and more contemporary visuals. Not an exact Super Hang-On clone, so purists will have to wait for a proper port of the real thing on PC. But this is probably the closest thing to it I've yet found on the platform. 

The game is a fun but fair challenge, and my failure to complete it has had more to do with my poor eyesight and low visibility under certain lighting conditions than anything else. Opponents are easy to see coming if you keep your eyes on the horizon, and if avoided consistently, it almost always means hitting checkpoints with seconds to spare. 

But on those dark courses, at later stages (which equates to more opponents,) sometimes I'm right on top of them before I can see them coming. And at course transitions, there are large text HUD elements that momentarily make viewing opponents a challenge as well. These visibility issues, while minor, are probably my only serious critiques of the game. 

A gamma adjustment for opponents (or just in general) coupled with a HUD-less mode and the ability to disable particles might be welcome changes in this game or in any prospective sequel.

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
The above notwithstanding, this is an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a fun game in this style at an exceptionally low price. It has that wonderful "zone out" quality that most of us who grew up with these kinds of games remember so fondly. Easily worth its price in my view.

Super Night Raiders is my first racing game that I've managed to finish. Actually, it isn't exactly a racing game - you aren't trying to be the 1st but complete laps under a given time, depending on the difficulty setting you choose. While you are driving you are encountering other freeway bikers which are supposed to be obstacles that you aren't supposed to hit - if you hit them you get a massive speed penalty which can ruin your run. One or two mistakes is actually ok, but if you do more than that you probably won't make it on the normal mode. Easy mode is exactly the same, except that it grants you more time to finish each lap so you are allowed to make more mistakes, but you don't get achievements. 

All freeway bikers, in every level, in each lap, appear at the exact same location. With letting go of your finger off the speed button for a fraction of second grants you great mobility to avoid those freeway bikers when you are making a turn. When you aren't making a turn it is very easy to avoid them. So, the game requires minimal skills, just time your turns and avoid the obstacles. However, there is a catch. Sometimes those obstacles -bikers- are put in a certain position, such as three or four showing up instantly on a curve with very little space to go through them, that it is very hard to immediately react to dodge them. But if you memorize the track -since they always appear at the same location on the road- especially when those dangerous encounters are supposed to appear, you can dodge them easily as well. So the game might require a little bit of track memorization too. 

Most of the levels are easy, there are 13 levels. Each of the 12 levels have 6 laps in total, and each lap takes about 25+ seconds or something to complete, 40+ secs in easy mode. However there is a special one with 36 laps which can be challenging and might require some memorization especially if you aren't good with your reflexes, because some obstacles require really tight maneuvering so you have to remember which laps are going to be dangerous.

Game is quite easy to learn, there isn't much depth to it, but it has a very cool retro feeling (there is also a 3D version if you don't like 2D) and I really like motorbikes so I totally loved this game.

Super Night Riders is a straight up, no-nonsense, oldschool motorcycle riding game.  I played using a game controller, but keyboard is also an option.  You bike as a stylistic blonde anime chick over one of six locations, trying to beat the clock without running into any other rider.  Starts out easy, gets hard towards the end.

- It reminded me of an upgraded version of HangOn! Or RoadRash, which were biker games around the dawn of console gaming.

There are two tracks to play: 
       Course: A 6 part scenery tour, which can be played on six levels of difficulty with a 7th course where you can play all 36 parts in one go.
       Stage: Each level is one location of scenery with six gates.  Each new location becomes more difficult.

There are two styles to play:
       Super: the graphics are smoothed out and prettier. 
       Classic: the graphics are oldschool. 

And there is an easy mode you can toggle on and off (being on easy mode removes the ability to earn achievements.)

- Super Night Riders also has a pretty nice soundtrack of gutteral guitars and anime vibes.  You can flip through each song during a ride or let it choose randomly for you.

- There are no cutscenes, upgrades, diff bikes, dramatic fall animations, or story here.  You're just playing to cruise and beat the clock in the simplest of terms.  

- It seems kinda pointless to get the dlc for the cover character art when there's no real backstory for her, unless you make her your personal waifu and make one up or something.  I'm not one to judge.  Getting the soundtrack would be worth it on sale since there aren't many tracks.

- The difficulty seems to ramp up around the Canyon level (I think level 4/6)  in the Stage area.  It went from 'avoid the other bikers' to 'don't hit anyone and you can still lose anyway' and 'hitting one guy will be endgame' out of nowhere for me.  This made the game go from entertaining ride to irritating ride because I then got stuck.  Strangely enough, this wasn't an issue with the Courses, where the difficulty was challenging but consistent. 



In short, Super Night Riders is a nostalgic biker game that's both fun and a time killer.  It's not trying to be a huge title, and it's not perfect, but it's just right if you're looking for a quick ride.  I can't justify getting this full price, however.  So if you see it on sale, go for it.

When I first saw this game in here, I thought to myself: "Well, this sure reminds me of Outrun", which is simply one of my most favourite racing simulators ever. I mean, there're the different stages, music that you can get to choose, backgrounds etc... Then I read in one of the reviews that it was actually similar to "Hang On" and I think it's right; it's like a mix between both games? I wonder...

Anyway, so let's make an overall analysis: The game doesn't really has a story, but you take control of this blonde girl who's always racing against an endless amount of bikers throughout several different roads.

Since there's no story mode, there're two different modes that you can get to choose: Racing courses, which certainly reminds me about Outrun, with the sceneries transitions and everything and the courses, where you race in the same stage, but during a 24 hour period (this girl and every other biker in this game should be locked in jail for good).

Concerning the graphics, they're really incredible and the best thing is that they don't demand much of the card. There's even the "classic" mode available, which provides simpler sprites, but I didn't like much, because I think that the lightning effects somehow get mixed with the other racers and it can get a bit confusing.

The sound effects are decent, and the soundtrack has a good variety of music available, even though I must confess that at certain points, I've listened to songs from another games, such as "Lotus III", the everlasting DOS classic and even a little bit from Outrun 2006 C2C.

As for the gameplay, it's pretty much simple: One button to move forward, another one to break and two different sides in order to steer your motorcycle. As mentioned previously, there're those two different modes that you can get to choose from (each victory providing a specific achievement) and even an easy mode, but I didn't get to try to see how it is.

Ok, so at first, it seemed to me like an innocent casual game that you can get to play from time to time, and to be quite honest, it really is. I mean... That until you get to the "final level". To give you an example, imagine that you're a miner and every day you go to work and you easily extract ore while whistling with the sun shining on your face. Then, all of a sudden, everywhere around getting dark, then there's an avalanche, the mine starts to collapse and you find yourself running for your life while pissing in your pants. That's the kind of difficulty curve we're talking about.

Nonetheless, if you're persistent enough, I'm sure that eventually you're gonna get through that challenge with flying colors, unlocking every single achievement and celebrating like never before. Overall, it's an awesome game with a decent price, I just wished that it could be longer and with more content. I hope that the developers will release something like that in the future.
